properties.statement:
EDGE `evidence` AND `note` ARE PROSE WRITTEN AT A MOMENT IN TIME, EXACTLY AS PERISHABLE AS NODE TEXT, AND NO DETECTOR READS THEM. Measured in bhome, 2026-08-31 (art:bhome-genesis-feedback-2026-08-31, "Session 1, part 7").

THE INSTANCE, and it is a clean one. Anthony narrowed a climate requirement from desert-to-arctic to lower-48 city climates. `propagate_change` returned 53 impacted nodes with an 8-node direct ring, five of them RISKS edges pointing at the changed requirement — which the report calls the best single moment of the session, because those five objections had been written across three earlier conversations, hours apart, each as a brainstorm aside, and nothing else would have recalled them.

But the five RISKS edges carried `evidence` written when the range WAS desert-to-arctic — e.g. "in the arctic, a tank of water at fish temperature is a large continuous heat load". After the narrowing that evidence is WRONG, and a reader following the edge is misled by prose that reads as current. The agent repaired four of five by hand, and says why it caught them at all: "only because the propagation happened to list them and I happened to remember what they said."

🛑 THE ASYMMETRY IS THE FINDING. The node-level story is complete: every `add_*` warns loudly on overwrite, `reconcile_artifacts` catches design-vs-file drift, `change_axis_unstated` catches an unstated axis. The edge-level story is empty. Nothing warns, nothing reconciles, nothing detects. An edge property is a claim about the world in the same way a node property is, and only one of the two is governed.

⭐ THE REPAIR IS AVAILABLE WHERE THE DEFECT IS. `propagate_change` already computes the direct ring and already holds both the changed node's text and each ring edge's `evidence`. The report's own two proposals, cheapest first: ① when a direct-ring edge's `evidence` mentions terms that no longer appear in the changed node, say so — even a crude string check would have caught "arctic" surviving in four edges after "arctic" left the requirement; ② more generally a `stale_edge_evidence` detector, or a `written_at` stamp on edge prose so a reader can see the evidence predates the node it describes.

📌 NOT A WRITE PROBLEM: "Re-writing an edge with `create_edges` upserts its properties cleanly, which made the repair easy once identified — the problem is purely one of noticing."
